question: Bab el-Mandeb Strait effectively closed by July 31?
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if IMF PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls (“Arrivals of Ships”) for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait less than or equal to 10 for any date between market creation and the listed date. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market will resolve as soon as IMF PortWatch publishes a 7-day moving average of transit calls for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait equal to or below 10, or once data has been published for the listed date and no such value has been published.

If no data has been published for the listed date within 14 calendar days (ET) after that date, this market will resolve based on the data published up to that point.

Revisions to previously published data points made before data has been published for the listed date will be considered; however, they will not disqualify a previously published data point from qualifying. Revisions made after data has been published for the listed date will not be considered.

The resolution source for this market will be IMF PortWatch, specifically the “Arrivals of Ships” data published for the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/6b1814d64903461b98144a6cc25eb79c.

I'm writing up the findings now. I could only use sources dated on or before 2026-07-16, and most of what I found was published later, so I left it out.

# Bab el-Mandeb: will the PortWatch 7-day average hit 10 or less by July 31, 2026?

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-07-16: I could not get the IMF PortWatch page. The site, its ArcGIS data API and mirror sites (MacroMicro, El Estrecho Digital) all failed through my proxy. **So I can't report the latest 7-day average or its date.** [PortWatch](https://portwatch.imf.org/pages/6b1814d64903461b98144a6cc25eb79c)
- What counts: the 7-day moving average of "Arrivals of Ships" (transit calls) has to be at or below 10 on any date up to July 31. PortWatch is AIS-based (ship transponder data), so ships with transponders off are not counted.

## 2. Current status
- As far as I can tell, nothing has settled the question yet. I found no evidence of a reading at or below 10 before July 16.
- Undated, unverified: a summary of the Polymarket market says the 7-day average reached a low of **about 11 around June 23, 2026**, just above the threshold. I could not confirm this against PortWatch, and it conflicts with a third-party figure I couldn't date or verify that put the 2026 low much higher, around 24. Treat both with caution. [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-closed-by)
- May 2026: daily traffic was about 31 ships per day, against a pre-war level of about 75 (Wikipedia, citing May 2026). [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_Sea_crisis)

## 3. Recent news (newest first, up to July 16)
- ~2026-07-13 to 07-15: Strikes, which the Houthis blamed on Saudi Arabia, hit the runway at Sanaa International Airport. Yemen's government said the aim was to stop an Iranian plane from landing. The Houthis said the de-escalation period was over, threatened Riyadh's King Khalid Airport, and announced a "maritime embargo" on Saudi Arabia without saying what it would involve. They also threatened Red Sea oil tankers. [Fox News](https://www.foxnews.com/world/iran-backed-terror-proxy-houthis-threaten-fresh-attacks-after-yemen-airport-strike.print); [The New Arab](https://english.alaraby.co.uk/news/yemens-houthis-claim-new-drone-attack-saudi-airport); [Newcastle Herald](https://www.newcastleherald.com.au/story/9314342/houthis-declare-naval-blockade-against-saudi-arabia/)
- 2026-07-08: A Lloyd's List headline: "Fresh tanker attacks sharpen crude importers' Red Sea vs Hormuz dilemma." [Lloyd's List](https://www.lloydslist.com/LL1157089/Daily-Briefing-8-July-2026)
- Background for 2026: there is a US/Israel-Iran war, and the Strait of Hormuz is partly blocked. Saudi Arabia is sending crude through its East-West Pipeline to Red Sea ports, which raises the strategic weight of Bab el-Mandeb.

## 4. Base rates
- Since late 2023, traffic has stayed far below the 2023 baseline of about 70 ships per day, but the 7-day average has rarely, if ever, dropped to 10 or below. I could not confirm any reading at or below 10, even during the worst Houthi campaigns of 2024-25.
- In 2026 traffic has been in the 20s-30s per day (about 31 in May). The unverified ~11 reading in late June would be the closest it has come.
- To get to 10 or below, traffic would have to fall roughly 60-70% from a typical 2026 level of about 30 and stay there for a full week. Container and shadow-fleet traffic has historically kept moving even during heavy attacks.
- The Polymarket monthly series ("closed by April/May/...") exists, and I saw no sign that any earlier month resolved Yes, though I could not check each one directly.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I could not get current prices for the Polymarket "July 31" contract. The pages and the CryptoSlate and Orrery mirrors were blocked. [Polymarket](https://polymarket.com/event/bab-el-mandeb-strait-effectively-closed-by)
- Undated: Crypto Briefing reported 22% on Polymarket for closure by December 31, and said daily crossings had fallen to about 15 on some days. [Crypto Briefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/polymarket-bab-el-mandeb-strait-closure-odds/)
- A related Manifold market asks whether the 7-day average falls below 15 in 2026. I couldn't get its probability. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Xiphias/will-the-7day-moving-average-of-shi)

## 6. Upcoming events that could move the outcome
- How the threatened Houthi "maritime embargo" on Saudi Arabia is defined and enforced, which was announced but unclear as of mid-July. If they formally declare it, attack ships, or widen it to non-Saudi shipping, transits could drop sharply.
- Saudi or coalition retaliation after the Sanaa airport strike, and any Houthi missile or drone attacks on Saudi Arabia.
- The course of the US-Iran conflict and Hormuz: more Saudi exports going out through the Red Sea means more targets.
- Notices from UKMTO and JMIC (the maritime security agencies) and changes in war-risk insurance, which tend to lead rerouting decisions.
- Data quirks: AIS going dark and PortWatch revisions or lags. Data for July 31 should appear within days, and the deadline for publication is August 14.

**Main gaps:** I have no direct PortWatch reading as of July 16, no verified 2026 minimum, and no current Polymarket price for July 31. If you can reach the PortWatch chart or Polymarket yourself, those are the first things to check.
